note: Curated text for Z-Anatomy candidate pins. Descriptions are original AnatomyGo writing, checked against the listed references; Z-Anatomy's own definitions (largely from Wikipedia) were not copied. A feature is metadata-ready when it has a Latin name and a description. Existing landmark text is preferred at import when present and suitable.

grays1918.name: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray
grays1918.note: 1918 terminology differs in places (e.g. its 'acromial angle'); modern terms were checked against the extra references listed per feature.

Arytenoid cartilage|Colliculus of aryten.description: A small rounded rise on the front surface of the arytenoid cartilage, at the upper end of its arcuate crest.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx; Myology: cricoarytenoid muscles

Arytenoid cartilage|Muscular process.description: The short projection at the outer corner of the base of the arytenoid. The posterior and lateral cricoarytenoid muscles pull on it to open or close the vocal folds.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx; Myology: cricoarytenoid muscles

Arytenoid cartilage|Vocal process.description: The forward-pointing projection at the front of the base of the arytenoid. The vocal ligament, inside the vocal fold, attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx; Myology: cricoarytenoid muscles

Body of sternum|Sternal angle.description: The ridge where the manubrium joins the body of the sternum, easily felt on the chest. It lies level with the joints of the second rib cartilages, which helps when counting ribs.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sternum

Calcaneus|Anterior process of calcaneus.description: The forward projection at the front of the calcaneus, next to its joint with the cuboid. The bifurcate ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus
https://radiopaedia.org/articles/bifurcate-ligament

Calcaneus|Calcaneal tubercle.description: A small rounded bump toward the front of the underside of the calcaneus. The short plantar ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus

Calcaneus|Calcaneal tuberosity.description: The large rounded back part of the calcaneus that forms the heel. The calcaneal (Achilles) tendon inserts on its back surface.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus

Calcaneus|Lateral process of calcaneal t.description: The smaller projection on the outer side of the underside of the heel. Abductor digiti minimi starts partly from it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus

Calcaneus|Medial process of calcaneal tu.description: The larger projection on the inner side of the underside of the heel. Abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis and the plantar aponeurosis attach to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus

Calcaneus|Sustentaculum tali.description: A shelf projecting from the inner side of the calcaneus that supports the talus. The tendon of flexor hallucis longus runs in a groove beneath it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Calcaneus; Syndesmology: plantar ligaments; Myology: tendo calcaneus

Clavicle|Conoid tubercle.description: A small projection on the underside of the clavicle near its outer end. The conoid ligament, part of the coracoclavicular ligament, attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Clavicle

Clavicle|Tuberosity for coracoclavicular.description: The roughened area on the underside of the outer clavicle, made up of the conoid tubercle and the trapezoid line. The coracoclavicular ligament binds the clavicle to the coracoid process here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Clavicle

Cuboid bone|Tuberosity of cuboid bone.description: A ridge on the underside of the cuboid, just behind the groove for the fibularis longus tendon. The long plantar ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Syndesmology: The Long Plantar Ligament

Frontal bone|Frontal eminence.description: A rounded prominence on each side of the forehead, about 3 cm above the upper edge of the orbit. It is usually more pronounced in children.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Frontal Bone

Frontal bone|Glabella.description: The smooth, slightly raised area between the eyebrows, above the root of the nose. It is a standard reference point for measuring the skull.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Frontal Bone

Frontal bone|Nasal spine of frontal bone.description: A small downward projection in the middle of the nasal part of the frontal bone. It sits behind the nasal bones and forms a small part of the nasal septum.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Frontal Bone

Frontal bone|Zygomatic process of fronta.description: The strong projection at the outer end of the brow. It joins the zygomatic bone and forms the upper outer corner of the orbit.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Frontal Bone

Hip bone|Acetabular notch.description: The gap in the lower rim of the acetabulum. The transverse acetabular ligament bridges this notch.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Anterior inferior iliac spine.description: A rounded projection on the front edge of the ilium, below the anterior superior iliac spine and just above the hip socket. The straight head of rectus femoris attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Anterior obturator tubercle.description: A small projection on the pubis at the front edge of the obturator foramen. It borders the obturator groove, through which the obturator nerve and vessels leave the pelvis.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Anterior superior iliac spine.description: The prominent front end of the iliac crest, easily felt at the front of the hip. The sartorius muscle and the outer end of the inguinal ligament attach here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Greater sciatic notch.description: A deep indentation along the back of the hip bone, above the ischial spine. It helps form the greater sciatic foramen.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Iliac tubercle.description: A thickening on the outer lip of the iliac crest, a short distance behind the anterior superior iliac spine.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Iliac tuberosity.description: The rough area on the inner, back part of the ilium, above and behind its joint surface for the sacrum. It anchors strong sacroiliac ligaments.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Iliopubic eminence.description: A raised area where the ilium meets the superior ramus of the pubis. It marks the junction of these two parts of the hip bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Ischial spine.description: A pointed projection between the greater and lesser sciatic notches. The sacrospinous ligament attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Ischial tuberosity.description: The rough lower part of the ischium that bears weight when sitting. It also provides attachment for the hamstring muscles.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_bone

Hip bone|Lesser sciatic notch.description: The curved indentation below the ischial spine and above the ischial tuberosity. It helps form the lesser sciatic foramen.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Posterior inferior iliac spine.description: A projection on the back edge of the ilium, below the posterior superior iliac spine. It marks the upper end of the greater sciatic notch, near the lower part of the sacroiliac joint.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Posterior superior iliac spine.description: The bony prominence at the back end of the iliac crest. It lies near the sacroiliac joint and the lower-back dimples.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Hip bone|Pubic tubercle.description: A small bony prominence on the upper part of the pubis. The medial end of the inguinal ligament attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Hip Bone

Humerus|Deltoid tuberosity.description: A rough, raised area on the outer side of the humeral shaft, about halfway down. The deltoid muscle inserts here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Humerus

Humerus|Greater tubercle.description: The large projection on the outer side of the upper humerus. Supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor attach to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Humerus

Humerus|Lateral epicondyle of humerus.description: The smaller projection on the outer side of the lower humerus. The forearm extensor muscles share a tendon that starts here, and the radial collateral ligament of the elbow attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Humerus

Humerus|Lesser tubercle.description: A smaller projection on the front of the upper humerus, on the inner side of the intertubercular groove. Subscapularis attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Humerus

Humerus|Medial epicondyle of humerus.description: The prominent projection on the inner side of the lower humerus. The forearm flexor muscles share a tendon that starts here, and the ulnar nerve runs in a groove behind it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Humerus

Mandible|Genion.description: A measuring point at the tip of the mental spines, on the inner surface of the chin.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible
https://www.imaios.com/en/e-anatomy/anatomical-structures/genion-1536898944
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_spine

Mandible|Gnathion.description: A measuring point on the midline of the chin, halfway between its most forward and its lowest points.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalometric_analysis

Mandible|Inferior mental spine.description: A small projection in the midline of the inner surface of the chin, below the superior mental spine. The geniohyoid muscle attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible

Mandible|Mental protuberance.description: The triangular prominence at the front of the chin in the midline. It gives the chin its shape.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible

Mandible|Mental tubercle.description: A small raised point at each lower corner of the mental protuberance. Together with the protuberance it shapes the chin.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible

Mandible|Superior mental spine.description: A small projection in the midline of the inner surface of the chin. The genioglossus muscle of the tongue attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Mandible

Occipital bone|External occipital protub.description: The bump in the middle of the back of the skull, felt where the neck meets the head. The trapezius and the ligamentum nuchae attach around it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Occipital Bone

Occipital bone|Internal occipital protub.description: A projection at the centre of the inner surface of the occipital bone, where the ridges of the cruciform eminence cross.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Occipital Bone

Occipital bone|Intrajugular process of o.description: A small projection on the edge of the occipital bone's jugular notch. It partly divides the jugular foramen.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Occipital Bone

Occipital bone|Jugular process.description: A projection beside the occipital condyle that forms the back edge of the jugular foramen. The rectus capitis lateralis muscle attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Occipital Bone

Occipital bone|Pharyngeal tubercle.description: A small projection on the underside of the occipital bone, in front of the foramen magnum. The fibrous midline seam of the pharynx attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Occipital Bone

Parietal bone|Frontal angle of parietal.description: The front upper corner of the parietal bone, at bregma, where it meets the frontal bone and the opposite parietal bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Parietal Bone

Parietal bone|Mastoid angle of parietal.description: The back lower corner of the parietal bone, at asterion, where it meets the occipital bone and the mastoid part of the temporal bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Parietal Bone

Parietal bone|Occipital angle of parieta.description: The back upper corner of the parietal bone, at lambda, where it meets the occipital bone and the opposite parietal bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Parietal Bone

Parietal bone|Parietal eminence.description: The most rounded part of the outer surface of the parietal bone. It marks the point where the bone starts to form before birth.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Parietal Bone

Parietal bone|Sphenoidal angle of pariet.description: The front lower corner of the parietal bone, at pterion, where it meets the frontal bone and the greater wing of the sphenoid. A branch of the middle meningeal artery runs in a groove on its inner surface.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Parietal Bone

Radius|Dorsal radial tubercle.description: A small ridge on the back of the lower radius, also called Lister's tubercle. The tendon of extensor pollicis longus turns around it on its way to the thumb.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Radius; surface anatomy of the wrist

Radius|Pronator tuberosity.description: A rough area halfway down the outer surface of the radius. Pronator teres inserts here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Radius; surface anatomy of the wrist

Radius|Radial styloid process.description: The pointed lower end of the radius on the thumb side of the wrist, easily felt under the skin. Brachioradialis inserts near its base.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Radius; surface anatomy of the wrist

Radius|Radial tuberosity.description: An oval, roughened projection just below the neck of the radius. The tendon of biceps brachii inserts here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Radius; surface anatomy of the wrist

Scapula|Acromial angle.description: The corner where the outer border of the acromion turns into the spine of the scapula. It can be felt as a bony point at the back of the shoulder.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angulus_acromialis
https://www.imaios.com/en/e-anatomy/anatomical-structures/acromial-angle-1537018464

Scapula|Acromion.description: The flat projection at the outer end of the scapular spine, forming the point of the shoulder. It joins the clavicle and gives attachment to the deltoid and trapezius muscles.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Coracoid process.description: A hook-like projection from the upper edge of the scapula that points forward below the clavicle. Pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps brachii attach to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Deltoid tubercle.description: A small prominence on the lower lip of the scapular spine, toward its inner end. It marks the inner end of the deltoid muscle's attachment along the spine.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deltoid_tubercle_of_spine_of_scapula

Scapula|Inferior angle of scapula.description: The lowest point of the scapula, where its medial and lateral borders meet. It usually lies level with the spine of the seventh thoracic vertebra, and teres major attaches to its back surface.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Infraglenoid tubercle.description: A roughened area just below the glenoid cavity. The long head of triceps brachii attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Scapular notch.description: A notch in the upper border of the scapula, next to the base of the coracoid process. The suprascapular nerve passes through it, beneath the superior transverse scapular ligament.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Spinoglenoid notch.description: The notch between the outer edge of the scapular spine and the back of the glenoid. The suprascapular nerve and vessels pass through it from the supraspinous to the infraspinous fossa.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Superior angle of scapula.description: The upper inner corner of the scapula, where the superior and medial borders meet. Levator scapulae attaches along the border just below it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Scapula|Supraglenoid tubercle.description: A small projection just above the glenoid cavity. The long head of biceps brachii attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Scapula; Myology: Trapezius, Levator scapulae, Biceps brachii

Sixth rib|Angle of rib.description: The point near the back of the rib where its shaft bends forward and twists. A tendon of the iliocostalis muscle attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ribs

Sixth rib|Tubercle of rib.description: A small knob at the back of the rib, where the neck meets the shaft. Its joint surface meets the transverse process of the matching vertebra.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ribs

Sphenoid bone|Anterior clinoid process.description: The backward-pointing projection at the inner end of each lesser wing of the sphenoid. The tentorium cerebelli attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Posterior clinoid process.description: A small projection at each upper corner of the dorsum sellae, behind the pituitary fossa. The tentorium cerebelli attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Pterygoid hamulus.description: A small hook at the lower end of the medial pterygoid plate. The tendon of tensor veli palatini turns around it on the way to the soft palate.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Pterygoid notch.description: The gap between the lower ends of the medial and lateral pterygoid plates. The pyramidal process of the palatine bone fits into it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Pterygospinous process.description: A small projection on the back edge of the lateral pterygoid plate. The pterygospinous ligament stretches from it to the spine of the sphenoid.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Sphenoidal lingula.description: A small ridge of bone at the outer edge of the carotid groove, in the angle between the body and the greater wing of the sphenoid.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Spine of sphenoid bone.description: A small downward-pointing projection at the back of each greater wing of the sphenoid. The sphenomandibular ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Tuberculum sellae.description: The small rise in front of the pituitary fossa on the upper surface of the sphenoid body. It marks the front edge of the seat for the pituitary gland.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Sphenoid bone|Vaginal process of sphenoi.description: A thin plate that runs inward from the base of the medial pterygoid plate, under the body of the sphenoid. It meets the vomer and the palatine bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Sphenoid Bone; Syndesmology: sphenomandibular ligament

Talus|Lateral process of talus.description: A wedge-shaped projection on the outer side of the talus, below its joint surface for the lateral malleolus. The lateral talocalcaneal ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Talus; Syndesmology: talocalcaneal and deltoid ligaments

Talus|Lateral tubercle.description: The outer of the two tubercles on the posterior process of the talus. The posterior talofibular ligament attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Talus; Syndesmology: talocalcaneal and deltoid ligaments

Talus|Medial tubercle.description: The inner of the two tubercles on the posterior process of the talus. Part of the deltoid ligament of the ankle attaches to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Talus; Syndesmology: talocalcaneal and deltoid ligaments

Talus|Posterior process of talus.description: The projection at the back of the talus, formed by its lateral and medial tubercles. The tendon of flexor hallucis longus runs in the groove between them.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Talus; Syndesmology: talocalcaneal and deltoid ligaments

Temporal bone|Apex of petrous part.description: The inner tip of the petrous part of the temporal bone, which points toward the sphenoid. It forms an edge of the foramen lacerum.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Temporal Bone

Temporal bone|Mastoid process.description: The rounded projection behind the ear, felt just behind the earlobe. Sternocleidomastoid attaches to it, and it contains small air cells.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Temporal Bone

Temporal bone|Styloid process of tempora.description: A slender, pointed projection below the ear that points down and forward. Three muscles, including stylohyoid, and two ligaments attach to it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Temporal Bone

Third metacarpal bone|Styloid process of.description: A small projection on the back of the base of the third metacarpal, on its thumb side. Extensor carpi radialis brevis inserts beside it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Metacarpus

Thyroid cartilage|Inferior horn of thyro.description: The short downward projection at the back lower corner of each thyroid lamina. It forms a small joint with the cricoid cartilage.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Inferior thyroid notch.description: A shallow notch in the middle of the lower border of the thyroid cartilage.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Inferior thyroid tuber.description: A small projection on the lower border of each thyroid lamina, at the lower end of the oblique line.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Laryngeal prominence.description: The forward-projecting angle where the two thyroid laminae meet, felt in the neck as the Adam's apple. It is usually more prominent in men.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Superior horn of thyro.description: The long upward projection at the back upper corner of each thyroid lamina. The lateral thyrohyoid ligament connects it to the hyoid bone.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Superior thyroid notch.description: The V-shaped notch in the middle of the upper border of the thyroid cartilage, just above the laryngeal prominence.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Thyroid cartilage|Superior thyroid tuber.description: A small projection on the outer surface of each thyroid lamina, at the upper end of the oblique line.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Splanchnology: The Cartilages of the Larynx

Ulna|Coronoid process of ulna.description: A projection at the front of the upper ulna, forming the lower part of the trochlear notch. It fits into the coronoid fossa of the humerus when the elbow bends.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ulna; Syndesmology: elbow ligaments

Ulna|Olecranon.description: The large curved projection at the upper end of the ulna that forms the point of the elbow. Triceps brachii inserts on it.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ulna; Syndesmology: elbow ligaments

Ulna|Sublime tubercle.description: A small tubercle on the inner edge of the coronoid process. The anterior band of the ulnar collateral ligament of the elbow attaches here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ulna; Syndesmology: elbow ligaments

Ulna|Tuberosity of ulna.description: A rough area just below the coronoid process on the front of the ulna. Brachialis inserts here.
references: Gray H. Anatomy of the Human Body, 20th ed. (1918), public domain; archive.org/details/anatomyofhumanbo1918gray — Osteology: The Ulna; Syndesmology: elbow ligaments
